$comment: ONE golden fixture for the sibling sort, consumed by BOTH suites:
The tool and the sidebar must order siblings identically, because
chat_folder_tree is where an agent reads the sequence it then names a
before/after anchor in, so an anchor is only correct while the two agree.
This file is the single artifact that agreement is checked against:
divergence on EITHER side fails here.
Add a row rather than a per-side test when a new coercion question comes up.
Every value below is one JSON can actually hold, because the folder store is
read with a bare json.loads / JSON.parse and never schema-checked on the way

cases.name: a missing order key sorts as 0, not as name-only
duplicate orders fall through to the name tie-break, folded A-Z
cases.$why: A-Z folds through a literal table on one side and +32 arithmetic on the other, so no Unicode table is consulted and human-alphabetical order survives. Without the fold these would read Beta, Gamma, alpha (B=0x42 < a=0x61).

cases.name: an uppercase initial sorts by its letter, not ahead of every lowercase one
cases.$why: Chosen so the fold decides a real ordering rather than a tie: folded, Apple precedes apricot; unfolded, EVERY capital would precede every lowercase word and the sidebar of a legacy store (all siblings tied at 0) would read uppercase-first.

cases.name: a non-ASCII capital is left alone, since its fold is version-dependent
cases.$why: U+0130 lowercases to two code units in Python and the exact result has moved across Unicode versions. It is outside A-Z so neither side touches it.
cases.$note: U+0130 is 0x0130, past every ASCII letter, so it sorts after zebra on both sides. Folding it would move it to the front on one side only.

cases.name: the sharp s is outside A-Z, so it sorts after a plain s
cases.$why: This pair was the casefold-vs-lower case; with no fold it is decided by code unit alone (s=0x73 before U+00DF), which is identical on both sides and depends on no Unicode table.

cases.name: an astral name compares by UTF-16 code unit, not code point
cases.$why: emoji are astral and this repo auto-generates emoji folder icons, so this row is ordinary. U+1F600 is 0xD83D,0xDE00 in UTF-16 but 0x1F600 as a code point, and U+FFFD sits between the two orderings

cases.name: a lone surrogate is a name, not a crash
cases.$why: persisted JSON can hold an unpaired surrogate; a raise here aborts the whole sort and every folder tool with it
cases.$note: name_code_units builds the string from UTF-16 units on both sides. A raw \ud800 escape is legal JSON but strict parsers (Vite's) reject an unpaired surrogate, so the value cannot travel as a JSON string.

cases.name: a non-string name coerces falsily on both sides
cases.$why: Python str(x or '') empties false/0; JS must use || not ?? to agree

cases.name: a junk order reads as 0 on both sides
cases.$why: int('abc') raises in Python and is caught to 0; 'abc' - 0 is NaN in JS, which silently unsorts a comparator unless guarded

cases.name: orders past MAX_SAFE_INTEGER clamp to the same bound on both sides
cases.$why: Python ints are unbounded; JSON.parse collapses 2**53+1 and 2**53 to one value. Unclamped, Python orders this pair while JS reads it as a tie and lets the name decide -- inverting it. Clamped, both read the bound and both let the name decide.

cases.name: an order below -MAX_SAFE_INTEGER clamps to the negative bound
a string order is not a number on either side, so it reads 0
cases.$why: Matching int() against Number() per string is unwinnable -- Number('0x10') is 16 and Number('1e3') is 1000 where int() raises on both. Only a real JSON number is accepted, so the whole class reads 0 identically.

cases.name: string orders that the two languages parse differently all read 0
a fractional order truncates toward zero on both sides
cases.$why: int(2.5) is 2 and int(-2.5) is -2; Math.trunc matches, while a bare Number would keep the fraction and sort between the integers

cases.name: a bool order is not a number on either side
cases.$why: typeof true is not 'number' in JS; Python excludes bool explicitly because it is an int subclass that would otherwise read as 1

cases.name: a non-string name is empty rather than stringified
cases.$why: str({'a': 1}) is "{'a': 1}" but String({a:1}) is '[object Object]'; str(True) is 'True' but String(true) is 'true', and a capital T sorts before every lowercase letter
